- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending upward, model often underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to capture momentum.
- Model frequently overpredicts late-period (last 5–7 days) prices when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish; cap forecast at 1–2% below true outcome for final 5–7 days.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (e.g., 1.00 → 0.00), model often fails to adjust quickly; apply lagged correction: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence; if below, increase by 0.5–1% per day.
